Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. About The Role Harmattan AI is scaling its industrial footprint across France, Morocco, the United States and future production locations. We are looking for a Director Global Logistics to build and lead the logistics function supporting this growth. The role owns the movement of finished products from shipment readiness through customer delivery. This includes international transport, customs, dangerous goods, export-control execution, routing, forwarders and delivery performance. It is a global leadership role with strong operational responsibility and close interfaces with Production, Supply Chain, Quality, Legal, Programme teams and international customers. Responsibilities The Director Global Logistics will establish and manage a global logistics system that is compliant, scalable and operationally effective. The role will own customer delivery from release of the finished product through proof of delivery, including transport planning, Incoterms, shipment documentation, customs clearance and delivery visibility. It will also define and manage the global network of freight forwarders, carriers and customs brokers. A major part of the role is ensuring that export-control, dangerous-goods and customs requirements are integrated early into the delivery process rather than addressed only when goods are ready to ship. The Director will therefore work closely with Legal, Supply Chain and Production to anticipate licence requirements, routing constraints and transport risks. The role will establish common logistics standards, processes and KPIs across all production locations and deploy the logistics system into new factories and countries as Harmattan AI expands. The Director will also build the team and external partner network required to improve delivery reliability, lead time and logistics cost. Supply Chain owns material flow into and through Production. Global Logistics owns the controlled movement of released finished goods to the customer. The role covers: Customer delivery and international transport Customs and trade operations Export-control execution Dangerous-goods logistics Forwarder, carrier and broker management Global routing and logistics network design Shipment compliance and release Logistics performance and cost management Candidate Requirements Experienced international logistics leader who is comfortable operating in a fast-growing and highly regulated industrial environment. Significant experience in international logistics, preferably in defence or another highly regulated industrial environment, together with strong knowledge of customs, import/export processes, international freight, Incoterms and shipment documentation. Experience with dangerous goods, regulated shipments and licence-dependent export processes is important, as is experience managing freight forwarders, carriers and customs brokers. Strong operational judgement and ability to make clear decisions under delivery pressure while maintaining compliance. Experience building or scaling logistics processes across several countries or production locations would be a strong advantage. Comfortable working across Production, Supply Chain, Quality, Legal and customer-facing teams and able to build processes that remain practical as the organisation grows. Combines strong compliance discipline with a pragmatic operational mindset. Anticipates problems before they affect customer delivery, creates clear ownership and is comfortable building structures where processes are still evolving. Able to distinguish between what is legally required, what is operationally necessary and what can be simplified, while creating a global logistics organisation that can scale with the company. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

review_candidates.description: Job Requirements Education: Bachelor’s degree or above. Work Experience: Minimum 5‑years of server and Linux O&M experience, including at least 3‑years of hands‑on experience in GPU compute‑cluster or AIDC production environments. Practical background in GPU‑server deployment, hardware troubleshooting, Linux administration and compute‑node resource management. Prior experience maintaining GPU server fleets of 100+ nodes or equivalent‑scale HPC clusters is preferred. Core Skills: Familiar with GPU‑server architectures such as B300, GB200, HGX or DGX; capable of diagnosing hardware faults on GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch, NICs and memory modules. Proficient with BMC/IPMI/Redfish, BIOS, RAID and firmware administration. Expert in Rocky Linux / Ubuntu deployment, configuration, upgrade and troubleshooting. Knowledgeable about NVIDIA drivers, CUDA and Fabric Manager. Basic familiarity with storage systems including Ceph, Lustre and BeeGFS. Understand Kubernetes container orchestration and GPU resource scheduling. Experienced with monitoring stacks: Prometheus, Grafana, DCGM Exporter. Able to build automation workflows using Shell, Python or Ansible. Certification Requirements: Must hold a valid RHCE certification. Candidates with CKA, CKS or NVIDIA AI Infrastructure certifications are preferred. Other Special Requirements: Must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Able to work in both English and Chinese. Permitted to access computer rooms for cabling and on‑site troubleshooting.Key Job Responsibilities Complete GPU‑server receiving inspection, rack mounting, cabling, initialization, cluster onboarding and asset management. Diagnose hardware faults for GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch, memory and disks; coordinate component replacement and vendor RMA workflows. Manage full lifecycle for BMC, BIOS, firmware, Linux OS, NVIDIA drivers and CUDA. Conduct Linux configuration, patching, security hardening, log analysis and fault resolution. Perform day‑to‑day O&M, capacity planning and performance monitoring for Ceph, Lustre, BeeGFS storage systems. Collaborate with Shenzhen‑based teams on Kubernetes, Slurm, container operations, GPU scheduling and cluster incident resolution. Manage full lifecycle of servers and GPU nodes, and maintain compute‑resource inventory records. Coordinate with colocation facilities, server vendors and Shenzhen technical teams for emergency incident handling. Benefits: 401(k) Health insurance Language: Chinese (Required)
